messages:
dana: Quick heads-up — I spotted a couple of errors on the Troubleshooting -> "429s / timeouts / fallbacks" doc. The Python SDK retry example doesn't match current client behavior. Filing a tiny PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1234 :eyes:
will: @dana linking now. which part is wrong exactly?
dana: The snippet recommends `client.retries = 3` but our SDK uses `RetryConfig(max_attempts=3, backoff='exponential')` in the newest release. Also note we auto-defer to the fallback model on rate limit if route policy allows; the doc implies we always return 429.
will: ah ok. I'll update the snippet. Should we add a short table that maps 429 -> retry vs fallback behavior by deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)?
emily: yes please. Quick mapping from runtime: hosted = fallback supported (if configured), dedicated = usually queue/429 unless configured with fallback model, private = depends on customer policy. I can write the little table.
dana: perfect. Also add an explicit example showing how to detect a 429 vs a timeout in the SDK: `except HTTPStatusError as e:` then check `e.status_code` vs catching `TimeoutError`.
will: working on PR now. gonna replace the old python block with this code block — please sanity-check: ```python
from redwood import Client
from redwood.errors import HTTPStatusError

client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
try:
    resp = client.generate("summary of ...")
except HTTPStatusError as e:
    if e.status_code == 429:
        # client-level retry or fallbacks configured by routing policy
        handle_rate_limit()
    else:
        raise
except TimeoutError:
    # differentiate network timeouts vs server-side throttles
    handle_timeout()
```
emily: tiny nit — TimeoutError isn't always exported from lower-level libs; recommend `requests.exceptions.Timeout` or the SDK's documented `redwood.errors.TimeoutError`. Add a note.
dana: good catch. I'll add the specific symbol and link to SDK reference. Also adding a short note about token limits: show predicted truncated length and the `context_limit` warning payload we return.
will: CI triggered on the branch — deploy-bot reports checks: `deploy-bot: CI passed (docs build)`, but one link-check failed (broken link to old RFC). I'll patch that link in the PR.
deploy-bot: CI passed (docs build) — 4 checks, 1 warning (link-check). See https://ci.redwood.internal/12345
emily: after we merge, can someone add a short migration note to the 1.8 -> 1.9 SDK changelog? Folks who upgrade might still look for `client.retries`.
dana: will do. I'll drop a line in changelog and in the doc's callout: "SDK usage changed in 1.9".
will: pushed an update to the PR with the new table and corrected python snippet. @emily can you review the wording on fallback behavior?
emily: on it. will fix a phrase about "automatic fallback" -> "automatic fallback if routing policy allows it; otherwise client returns 429".
dana: awesome — thanks all. plan to merge after emily approves and link-check passes. :thumbsup:
will: merging after approval. thanks!
